name: Eddy currents in silicon
description: The last plate's carriers flew far between collisions, so that the field turned their paths by a good part of a radian on the way ($\omega_c \tau \approx 0.4$; the Scales section). This plate is lightly doped silicon's: its carriers collide far more often, in a field that swings faster. The field barely turns them between collisions ($\omega_c \tau \approx 0.05$), so the eddy currents follow Ohm's law alone, as they do in copper at any laboratory field, and their heat grows as $B_0^2$. Set the swing $B_0$ so that the plate takes between 1 and 4 of heat per unit time (averaged over $t = 25$ to $125$).

reality.represents: Eddy currents in Ohm's regime, as in copper

remarks.detail: The field barely turns the carriers between collisions (ω_c τ ≈ 0.05), the swing is slow against them, and the heat grows as B₀², as in copper at any laboratory field.
The plate's own ratios are lightly doped silicon's; copper's (400 plasma oscillations per collision) are beyond the model, and only its regime is reproduced.

The carriers' currents make no magnetic field of their own: no self-inductance and no skin effect, valid while the skin depth is far larger than the conductor. The only magnetic field is the solenoid's.

Carriers bounce off randomly placed hard discs and leave with a fresh thermal speed; the lattice takes the heat and never warms. Real carriers scatter off lattice vibrations and impurities at rates that depend on energy and temperature.

electrodes.label: inert electrode (floating, emits nothing; the model needs one)
